author: Nat’s Take

title: Not ADHD friendly. Just ADHD targeted.
body:
I downloaded this app because it specifically advertised itself as being ADHD friendly. Unfortunately, my experience was the complete opposite.

The onboarding is filled with endless text and screens to click through, which is already overwhelming. Then you’re encouraged to subscribe with just a couple of taps, but cancelling is an absolute nightmare. Some subscriptions are sold as bundles, others separately, and the cancellation process constantly redirects you between different pages and apps. The layout makes it incredibly easy to accidentally close the page or lose your place and start over.

For an app targeting people with ADHD, this design feels particularly frustrating. It isn’t ADHD friendly at all. If anything, it takes advantage of the exact executive functioning difficulties it claims to help with. Whether intentional or not, the result is the same: cancelling becomes so exhausting that many people may simply give up.

I also found the pricing strategy misleading. The app initially suggests that money shouldn’t stand in the way of improving your life and advertises a plan for around $2. But once you’re invested, you’re presented with subscriptions ranging from $40 to $60. That feels like a bait and switch rather than transparent pricing.

And lastly, loads and loads of AI generated content. For these prices there should be human made content available. 

I genuinely hope the developers reconsider both the subscription flow and the user experience. An app designed for people with ADHD should reduce cognitive load, not increase it.

title: Misleading, Confusing, Unauthorized Charges — AVOID THIS APP
body:
Edit: I successfully filed a dispute for a charge back with my bank. Once the bank submitted the charge back I received an email from them. It basically said they wanted to ‘help me’ directly and provide a refund. lol and they wanted to know why I filed a dispute instead of reaching out for support, I reached out to customer service multiple times and they continually closed my case without helping me. In my final email to them I told them I was going to file a dispute and got no response. 

I signed up for a $1.39 trial through their website, not the App Store. It seems intentional—they lure users away from Apple/Google subscriptions because it’s much harder to manage or cancel. I cancelled the trial immediately, yet I was still charged $55.99 multiple times for a bundle of apps I never downloaded or authorized.

The subscription process is extremely confusing. I’m still unsure whether I am actually cancelled, and there is no easy way to confirm or manage it. The charges are not visible in standard device subscription settings, and customer service has been unhelpful and refused to provide documentation or explanation, closing my case without resolving the issue.

I have never received or used any of the services I was charged for. Many other users have reported the same deceptive practices online.

This app seems designed to trick users into paying for services they didn’t agree to. If you value transparency, control over your subscriptions, and peace of mind, avoid this app entirely.

tldr:  Cancelled after $1.39 trial, still charged $55.99 multiple times for apps I never downloaded. Confusing, deceptive, and customer service refused to help—avoid!

You cannot reach a real person,emails trigger automated responses that force you to click links and upload files just to raise a concern.This process feels intentionally designed to discourage complaints. There is no personal reply no accountability and no meaningful help after canceling. I was still refused a refund. I estimate this app has quietly taken hundreds of dollars from me through non-transparent billing. For an app that market itself as supportive with people with ADHD as they do have another app for that (the same developer). Instead of making life easier. Avoid this app unless you are comfortable with hidden charges bots instead of humans and a complete lack of customer focus support.

body: Love this app so much.  It has many different features that i find useful! There is a whole community on there if you need help from others going threw the same thing. I even love that you can go back to check mark things in the pass in case you forgot to be keeping track but still want to track your progress. I think it’s great that they add a learning and informational aspect to there program making it better that just your average habit tracker which help you developer skills and a mind set to over come difficulties. I admit I haven’t always stayed on tray but they’ve added a new service that I’m interested in trying that involves a personalized routine and coach for what’s going on in your life right now. It’s fun that they keep track of your streaks I find it motivating but also that they have little freeze rewards so even when you miss a day it preserves your streak while also promoting that just because you missed a day or two doesn’t mean everything stops. You just get back on track because consistency is more important than being perfect. We are only human after all. It’s fantastic that you can make as many lists as you want the only thing is I wish that they was an area I can see everything on my lists in one place because sometimes it gets annoying/ overwhelming to look into each list and sometimes I forget things because I didn’t look at each individual  list but I still like to have them separate to have it organized. Maybe it’s a feature the fabulous team will look into developing in the future :D Also would love for you guys to bring back the lifetime subscription.

title: Fabulous Meilleur investissement de 2025
body:
Fabulous est basé sur la science! Les neurosciences 🧠
Fabulous m’aide au quotidien depuis 2 mois. C’est la première fois de ma vie, en 36 ans d’existence, que j’ai une routine! C’est magique 🪄

Je pensais que c’était impossible pour moi de réussir cet exploit si insignifiant pour les adultes neurotypiques.

Pour être exact, je n’ai pas une routine: j’ai 3 routines!

Fabulous me suggère une routine pour le matin, le midi et le soir.

J’ai fait plusieurs essais avant de trouver l’ordre qui me convient pour les étapes de mes 3 routines. J’ai maintenant un rythme que je suis capable de tenir tous les jours.

Jamais je n’aurais pas être #thatGirl. La femme qui est capable de tenir un journal quotidien.

Comme femme TDAH je sais à quel point tenir un journal m’aide à avoir les idées claires.

Comme femme bipolaire, je sais à quel point un journal d’humeur est utile pour [essayer] de prévoir les manies et les dépressions.

J’ai découvert que, comme la plupart des gens, le concept de « strikes » me motive. 

Les personnes TDAH ont un manque chronique de dopamine. C’est mon cas.

En 2 mois je n’ai réussi aucune strike pour la tâche [Fil dentaire] 🦷. Je lâche pas!

Si ça fonctionne pour le yoga, les étirements quotidiens et la course 🏃🏾‍♀️ j’ai confiance que je vais réussir pour le Fil dentaire au moins 3 journées d’affilée.

Vraiment Fabulous est mon meilleur investissement de 2025. Peut-être même à vie… qui sait 🤔

Ce qui fait le succès de Fabulous à mes yeux c’est l’esthétisme de l’app 🎨

Le design UX/UI est abouti.
J’ai trouvé un seul bug mineur qui ne m’a jamais empêché d’utiliser l’app.

Les citations sur fond de décor de la nature ne sont pas ketaines. Les citations de personnes inspirantes sont toujours pertinentes.

Fréquemment je prends une capture d’écran de l’infographie ou de la citation du jour.

Fabulous propose régulièrement de partager à nos proches. C’est du marketing, certes, mais selon moi un bon marketing.

J’ai personnellement utilisé la fonction Partager pour inviter un ami dans mon défi [1 minute d’étirements].

J’ai aussi partagé le défi [Travail avec un partenaire] avec une amie qui est travailleuse autonome. 

Fabulous m’aide à être une meilleure personne. Pour moi-même. Pour mes proches. Et pour mes collègues et mes boss!

Fabulous à été créé pour les personnes TDAH. Comme femme autiste Fabulous m’aide au quotidien également.

Je souffre de ARFID. Fabulous m’aide à manger sur une base régulière. 

Les questions prompts comme [Quels est mon aliment sain préféré?] m’aide à identifier mes « safe foods ».

Très utile pour préparer mon premier RDV avec le nutritionniste. 

Merci aux créateur.ices de Fabulous 🙏🏼 
Grâce à vous, ma vie va bien. 😌 Bien mieux.

title: They refused to refund- Now I can't buy groceries.
body:
I tried out this app, because it was advertised on Instagram. The sign-up process was long, but I went through the whole rigmarole to see what it was like hoping for good tips. I was already hesitant when they asked for a 1-2$  for the 'trial' period before committing to a full subscription, but I thought "I'll try it for today and worse comes to worse, I'll be out 1$" 
I gave it the day, and it wasn't for me, but I didn't think much of it and proceeded to cancel my subscription. 

Cut to me checking my bank account today, and finding an unexpected charge of $84 to a 'fabulous subscription.' Bewildered, I logged in with my details and found my page said "your subscription ended January 25" (1 month prior) 

Feeling stressed as this was not money I could spare, I reached out immediately to fabulous to request a refund for the subscription I had not used since the trial-period.

I included a screenshot of the login screen clearly showing that my subscription was no longer active since January 25. 

The support team responded with no explanation other than to state they would not be giving me a refund. I have since requested that this be escalated.

title: THIS APP IS A SCAM
body:
I signed up for a $2 trial of this app, canceled weeks before renewal, and still was charged $83. I have screenshots proving my cancellation: an email on January 16 and a confirmation on January 24. Yet, the company claims I didn’t cancel on time, citing their T&Cs.

After doing some research, I discovered many others have reported similar issues—unsolicited charges even years after canceling. It appears they are taking advantage of people with ADHD and other vulnerable users by billing without proper notice.

I urge anyone considering this service to proceed with extreme caution. Read all terms carefully, and be prepared to dispute unauthorized charges if necessary. This experience has been both frustrating and financially harmful.

After one month (totally forgot about them) I got charged for the annual membership. 
I checked again in my App Store and nothing. So I researched online, downloaded the app again and I discovered  that you must go on their website to cancel (neither on the app is possible!!). 
I emailed the customer service explaining that I never used and I don’t use the app so I ask them to cancel my membership and refund me the annual fee but they just answered NO because everything is “legal” and I agreed to subscribe after the trial period. 
This is the clear sign that the developers and the company are definitely just about your money and they are not here to “help people” as they say. If you guys need the money from someone who doesn’t want your app you definitely are a poor company. 
RECAP: They do everything difficult to not make you unsubscribe and even if you ask immediately the refund they refuse to do it. Shame!

Whatever has happened over the last couple years has turned this into a frustrating app to use. title: Don’t do it
body:
Read carefully all the other 1 star reviews. This company wants more than anything to trick you into a year-long subscription and then inform you that it is NON-REFUNDABLE. It doesn’t matter that you are contacting them immediately after you got charged, doesn’t matter if you no longer need or want this app, and that you weren’t even aware you were subscribed. Their response is basically “sucks to be you, you should’ve read our terms and conditions, no?”

They use numerous strategies to achieve this. It’s incredibly hard to cancel. The subscription may not show on your Apple Store account making you think it’s been cancelled successfully. But no. You will still get charged. You have to find their website (which you have never seen before) and somehow you have a subscription there. Even there, the cancellation process is once again designed in such a way to make you think you cancelled half way through but you have to keep looking for that tiny “confirm cancellation” button which will be hidden at the bottom of the screen. It is designed that way on purpose. 

Just stay away from this app.

title: Needs Some Improvement
body:
I like some things about this app like the ability to maintain lists of habits. The graphics and sounds are cute but they need more variation over time as the reward value decreases otherwise. The daily coachings are ok and occasionally great, however mostly it’s unoriginal content based on well-known quotes.

Downsides: App is confusing to navigate, can sign up for challenges but then I can’t find the content. Misses opportunities to be more flexible and inclusive for a diverse range of people, abilities, schedules and preferences (for example exercise journey immediately pushes running on Tuesday, Thursday and Sunday. Why? Probably because that specific exercise routine works for the developer.) I’m on my third journey and 3/3 don’t fit well for my body or my life. I’m sticking to my habit goals anyway but thinking of moving away from using the app even though I have 10 months left on my premium subscription. Something I really don’t like is that they use a lot of space on your home page to advertise their other apps which aren’t relevant for my goals.

Recommend giving this one a miss. Had hoped for more given that it grew out of research AND is not cheap.

Par contre, je reproche énormément à l'application d'autant mettre d'importance sur la perte de poids. Le sport, l'alimentation et boire plus d'eau, devrais être fait non pas pour perdre du poids, mais pour être en santé. Certaines personnes ne veulent pas perdre de poids ou s'acceptent tout simplement comme ils sont. Je ne trouve pas cela très sain de mettre autant d'importance sur le poids et non pas uniquement sur la santé. Outre ce point, il devrait être possible de revenir une journée en arrière pour cocher les différents objectifs que l'on à réaliser, mais oublié de marquer comme étant fait. Pour finir, la section de l'istant fabulous manque vraiment de contenu. Malgré les défauts énoncés, j'aime beaucoup l'application, car cela m'aide énormément à réaliser mes objectifs et à rester motivé et je vais sans aucun doute continuer à long terme à l'utiliser.

title: Useful, but…
body: I really enjoy how Fabulous helps you to slowly and steadily build habits so they actually stick! I tend to try to rush through things or do too much all at once so that is very useful and actually has helped me stick with my morning routine. A+ for that aspect! What I find annoying is the insistence on using the stories of famous figures to motivate me. Especially when there’s no clear link between the habit and a benefit, like xyz ran and then and got fit. Otherwise it feels like they’re implying that the habit somehow made these people famous/rich/successful. It reminds me of all the stories about CEOs that wake up at 4 am so you should too, when 1) waking up at 4 am will not make me a millionaire and 2) our lives are drastically different anyway! Anyway, to sum up, I wish the makers of this app would cut down on the inspirational letters and community posts that feel like bad motivational posters and focus more on the behavioural science part.

title: Stolen money
body:
Just like the other reviews say, this app will trick you into an annual fee and won’t provide a reminder when (a whole year later!) your account is charged again. Most tech companies will issue a refund if you clearly haven’t used the program in a year. Not this one! If you haven’t set yourself a calendar reminder for a year in advance, you’re on your own! I regularly check my Apple subscriptions to make sure I won’t be charged for something I’m not using, but be warned: this app won’t show up in your Apple subscriptions — it’s separate. I’ve spoken to customer support (of course!) there’s nothing they can do.

They say they provide “information to manage your subscription,” but in 2022, it’s just not good enough. We’ve all got a bunch of subscriptions. We don’t automatically remember something we trialled 12 months ago. You can upset customers the “terms and conditions” spiel all you like, but in the meantime, you’re burning your reputation.

Fabulous, if you’re listening: clearly people are upset at the way these subscriptions are being managed. If you’re going to have them operate outside the App Store, the least you can do is let people know (12 months later!) when their subscription is about to be renewed. Or, failing that, give a completely inactive user back their money when they’ve been charged for a whole new year. Other tech companies do both of these things. It’s standard. And when you don’t — well — you end up with reviews like these. Eventually they’ll pile up and outnumber the good.

Conclusion: don’t bother with this app. They’re not interested in self-improvement — they’re interested in tricking inactive users into subscriptions.

And Fabulous, if you’re planning on replying, don’t bother apologizing. Just tell us how you plan on fixing your policies.

title: Do free trials like this 2B 💯 SAFE 😊
body:
AFTER downloading app & free trial I read reviews and got terrified they’d take the whole amount from me. I’m not sure but I think was around $65 1 time fee BUT as a Canadian I’m wondering if that price would go up 50% more or wtv exchange rate is rn⁉️I’d like to know cuz I’m thinking about buying it IF not.( Def not for $80+.)
   
Anyways to get back to the scary reviews….I get what they’re saying-it’s def annoying. BUT if u do this u should be fine. Works 4 me.  
📌After I finish signing up I set 📱 alarm for an hour or 2 later to remind me to 🚨📌go back into my  🍎 settings➡️subscriptions & IMMEDIATELY CANCEL IT‼️Same day‼️ That way I 💯% KNOW I won’t be charged.  This works because even after you cancel you still get to freely use all apps until the next pay period (aka trial ends) comes due.  This has worked on @least 5-6 different apps I’ve tried it on.

  Also, FYI, I contacted these ppl when I was panicking just to be sure b4 I used this new method & I found they were very helpful.   It’s SOO easy to forget to go back in days later & cancel.  I put everything in my calendar & set 2 different alarms to remind me days in advance for most things too.  Took off 2 stars for high price & only 1 week free trial otherwise I loved it for the few days I got to try it out.  Would’ve probs bought if had 2-3 weeks to get hooked. Too bad.

title: When there’s a will there’s a way. When there isn’t there’s an excuse.
body:
If you can commit to open this app a few times a day, you can change your life. If you want to ignore the notifications, it’s just as easy too. Your choice. 

It’s a fabulous app for those who want to change but need a steady source or encouragement and direction. I have POTS/Dysautonomia and it’s incredibly debilitating. It’s important to my chronic illness to complete many maintenance tasks in a day, starting with drinking water. This app is the gentle guiding force that dismantles all self doubt that I can build a fabulous daily routine and increase my quality of life. No gimmicks, just a lot of behavioural science and creativity from the creators to help you reach your goals. The only initial thing I had to cement into my mind was to open this app first before socials. 

The app is incredibly user friendly and has many customization options to suit your needs. It encourages you to build momentum and has an incredible amount of content to address the roadblocks you inevitably will cross to reach any goal. There’s no other app like this. Trust me I’ve looked. I now look forward to checking in and improving my life, one day at a time, one step at a time.

Fabulous has become an integral part of my allied health team.

title: Not practical and is set up to keep you subscribed
body:
I like the idea of it, I like it’s mission, and I generally  like the art. However, the app is set up in a way to keep you on the app which ultimately lowers your productivity (and is kind of just frustrating). You can’t just use it to organize your tasks and set goals, it makes you go through additional time consuming pop ups each time you do anything within the app. You can’t actually customize it as much as you think. It won’t let you uncheck tasks accidentally and also mostly keeps to its own structure.It also throughout the day it sends you way too many notifications.

Further now that I am trying to delete my account, there is nowhere to delete it - or at least it is hidden. title: Not accessible for Deaf people
body:
While the materials are amazing, and I know they are resourceful for many; I am often finding that I cannot participate in the coaching or meditative sessions because they are all audio based. 

What I would recommend is to include captions for all sessions, regardless if it is audio or not. Just by providing captions, it includes EVERYONE! There are countless of benefits to captioning your material- for those with ADHD, processing issues, aging adults (hard of hearing), and many others.

I truly hope someone reads this and makes changes to this app and make it amazing for everyone!

title: Helps With Depression!
body:
As someone who has lived with depression for 25 years, this app helps keep me on track! 
I also adore checking tasks off of my to-do list, so it’s rewarding to complete tasks for my mental and physical health. 
Considering it costs $60 ish/ year, and prescriptions that only cover up the symptoms instead of addressing them cost that amount monthly, I’m happy with this investment. 
I haven’t discovered all aspects of the app yet, but I appreciate how it will train you for things like yoga or exercise. I’m also looking forward to listening to the bedtime stories when my eyes are too heavy to read. 
Overall, this is my favourite app to come out so far (ever) and if you’d like to address any motivation issues in your life, give it a try! There’s a 1 week free trial, then you pay in advance for the year, so if this app isn’t for you, just remember to cancel it on day 6! But I won’t be as I’ve already noticed a significant change in my mental health and behaviour!

title: Great Way To Adopt Some Healthy Habits While The World Burns
body: This app won’t really fix the world’s problems, but if you struggle to do basic life stuff and/or have mental health concerns that affect your motivation, it’s very helpful on your personal journey to regain some control over the chaos. Don’t bother if you don’t like structure. The whole app is designed to create an illusion of structure and routine while we march towards our inevitable demise as a species. As we found out these past couple of years, the apocalypse  is not exciting nor fast. Unlike what Warner Brothers had us believing, we now know it’s just a slow slide into confusion; while petty men fight for supremacy, people die of a mysterious virus and the rain forests burn. However, while that’s playing out, you may as well eat regular meals, drink enough water, keep your house clean, stay fit and meditate. Just be the best person you can be on a personal level! I may offsets the literal dumpster fire that we are as a collective!?!?! Can’t hurt right? Unless you hate being bossed around my a computer. I figure, might as well get used to it. Also, I heard if we help the robots while they are taking over, they will treat us fairly in their new world order. Long live the mother board!

body: Starting, Finishing, and Maintaining are the hardest parts of any task, especially the journey to self-healing. title: Keep coming back to this
body: This is the best app I’ve used in terms of staying on top on the things I wish to do. Tbh I haven’t used it constantly and properly and kinda paid for three yrs subscription so far where I might’ve used it for 2 month overall. The reason is myself and once I stop following something for a few days I usually put it away and never go back to it. However, I keep subscribing to this app because when I do use it, I feel so much better and become more productive but mostly my mental health improves super fast. I realized later on this app is more focused on the mental health than being organized and when I found out it was an added bonus for me. Also, I’ve always wished there was someone to tell me what to do next. Someone to watch over me and I feel this app is the closest thing I’ve come across in my entire life. I never write reviews for any app, but I felt if I was looking at this, I would’ve appreciated such a  comment instead of a completely black or white reviews. So to finish, it is a great app if you can stick to it. If you’re not sure try to imitate it with a very small thing and if you felt you’re ready to follow through then subscribe. But if you’re like me and paying the cost makes you come back to it and follow the steps and money isn’t an issue then go ahead with it. And one more thing, I’ve only subscribed to another two apps in my entire life. I try to find free stuff and barely pay for such a thing, but I believe this will change my life so I keep it. I hope it can change your life for better too. :)

title: Hated it
body:
ADHD? = you will probably hate it and yourself, while trying to squeeze your fabulous neurodivergent self into their very neurotypical confining boxes! 

 As a person with adhd, it was too slow and without real “meaning”. If they added an option to speed up the coaching timing; then I might have been able to stick with it..maybe. I found myself reading through the readings just to keep focused cuz otherwise I would have tuned out from the sheer slowness of the speaking. 

It came down to “I will have to manual input all my routines” as I didn’t find any of the options were ones I was interested in, or related to. For me, tasks have to be specific, relevant, broken down and timed to have any relevance to me. And this app delivered none of that in their programming. And I searched through all the options to really try to find something that might be useful. 

And I think I’m deleting the app before they start charging me for it, as if I’m just using the shell of the app to create my own, which I’ve already been doing in my calendar, timers etc.. what am I even using this app for?

title: Save yourself the trouble and skip this App
body:
I rarely write reviews but am hoping to save someone else the trouble...

I downloaded this apps free trial and wasn’t a big fan of the overall experience. I cancelled my free trial of 7 days and then instantly received the typical wait - don’t go try a full 30 days for free. So I figured what the heck, maybe I didn’t give it a fair shot. I accepted the email offer which brought me back to the app. Fast forward 7 days later and I’m still not feeling it. I check my phone subscriptions and it is listing the application as cancelled. So I go ahead and delete the app. 3 weeks later I get a $50 charge to my credit card. No emailed receipt or anything. So far I have tried to contact customer service and haven’t been able to speak to an actual human.

This company is clearly cashing in on users by extending their “free” trials... As someone who is a regular app subscriber even if this was the absolute best app out there (which it isn’t) I cannot recommend promoting shady business practices.

title: Beautiful. Holistic. But confusing structure.
body:
I am writing here moreso to make two suggestions to the design team (see further below)

My review after 1 week of use. PROs:  this app really holds your hand to see through that your meet your commitments or objectives (support circle, affirmation, self-feedback,  journey map, baby steps, meditative sounds etc) and all this without being overwhelmed. Other self help apps seem incomplete, simple check boxes, not proactive, and just not as fun or visually appealing. CONs: The interface is heavy / convoluted and this makes it a bit confusing what to look for. It isn’t clear what is being asked of you which took me a few days to actual get the routine ball rolling. I’m also not a fan of the 7-day trial then get charged - I would prefer to be asked before being charged at the very least, or have a simple always free version of the app. 

Other Suggestions to the designers :
1)  Frontpage should be simple, with no need to scroll down. It should showcase an action point. The task/goal in the moment should be clear and ready to tick off. 
2) It would be helpful to see all the services this app has (list) in one place, and how the sequence, to better understand options, and steps needed or as extras. This could be a walk through or in a support page... 
3) It would be nice to have the meditative sound be an actual alarm to wake up to, as such we would dive right into the apps morning routine. 
4) You offer 7 day trials and 30 day trials to users, why not just do 30 days? And why not provide a notification to say trial is up, with the option to buy or not. (See my review above for rational). 
5) Notifications and clarity of steps can be improved to ensure one follows the routine. I suggest looking as Duolingo for inspiration. 
6) Option to automatically add a time for routines in the calendar would be a great addition. 

Thanks for a fabulous looking and engaging self help app!

title: 5 star app, 1 star communication
body: The app itself is just what I was looking for and it works even better than I had hoped. The customer service and transparency in communication is another story. After you sign up for the 7 day free trial you will get an email offering a 30 day guest pass. This 30 day trial is a new, *second* trial. It feels like you’re just filling out a form to unlock the 30 day extension. In reality you’re signing up again. So, you now have a 7 day trial from the App Store, and a 30 day trial from the website. You will be charged twice if you don’t cancel one of them. I emailed them after I was charged for the 7 day trial expiring. I asked them what happened to my free month? It took them two weeks to respond, after I followed up on Instagram, and only then did they explain that it’s a completely different trial and they deliver the news as if it’s your misunderstanding. I’m lucky I was able to cancel the second subscription in time. I’ll be keeping the iOS subscription because I really need this app and it’s doing wonders for me. But a word of caution about the experience.

title: I’m stingy with reviews but...
body: This app is deserving of a very positive review. Daily coaching, mental health check-ins, fitness prompts, healthy eating suggestions, reminders to drink water and brilliantly written and fun story telling to wrap it all together; The Fabulous has it all! This app has become something I look forward to in under three days because I really needed something that tied all of my goals together in a functional and accessible way. The “Make Me Fabulous” tab is my favourite thing ever right now, it has everything I need to keep me grounded throughout the day and I’m excited to see how adding these routines to my daily rituals will impact my life in the long run. I’d love to see more yoga, meditation, journal prompts and bedtime stories for premium in the future 🤞 the journal prompts in “sit and think” were particularly enjoyable and grounding. I’m really looking forward to what The Fabulous team will produce next! Thanks :)

title: Defeats its own purpose
body:
The app is cluttered, overly complicated, and not intuitive to navigate. Feels like it’s trying to be ten different apps. Very little can be accessed without spending money for the subscription. 

Perhaps it’s just not for me, but reinforcing new habits and making progress on personal goals is hard enough on its own, without having to keep track of challenges and badges and constantly receiving “secret letters” of generalized encouragement. 

It also feels like more screen real estate is dedicated to getting you to try new things than to help with whatever “journey” you’re on at the moment. Almost every page has new challenges to suggest. There are an overwhelming number of features that don’t seem to be organized in any particular way:

On “Home” it shows you some new challenges above your habit check list. 

In the “Journey” tab it suggests a new challenge before showing you your progress on individual habits.

 In “Launch” it shows you what % of your journey is complete, what challenges you could do next, and other journeys you could do next (a journey is collection of challenges). It also has a sub-page called “Make Me Fabulous” with a giant pile of unrelated things - a nap timer, a work timer, nature sounds, bedtime stories, guided meditation, guided stretching, guided exercise, inspirational podcasts...

In “Discover” there are more podcasts. Maybe the same ones? They might be 3 minutes or 25 minutes. They give you no indication of what they’re about, just a title - for example: “The Mindbus.” And underneath the podcasts - a bunch more challenges. 

It is exhausting to use this app! Save your money.

title: I love this
body:
I’m on day 3 of my fee trial and have already decided to pay for the premium version.

I am an online personal trainer and life coach and will be referring all my clients to this as well.  (I’ve only ever referred them to one app in the past and that is Insight Timer for their meditations. I love that we can add Fabulous to their toolbox!)

Clearly a LOT of thought, effort and love was put into this program by compassionate mental health professionals. 

As for the reviews that claim this app is a scam, they are so wrong. First off, this is a (small) investment into yourself. You’re worth it. It is clearly stated that you’re signing up for a free trial which you can cancel at any time before the 7th day. I think there’s a free version you can switch to, but I’ll be paying for premium. 

Imagine- you go to school and work for years towards your degree or doctorate in psychology. You then pour your heart and soul into creating an awesome app to help people based on years of education. You pay hundreds of thousands of dollars to develop an app that changes peoples lives (fabulous), people benefit, and then turn around and try and drag you down because they have to pay for it. Guys!!! This isn’t your mamas house!! I feel so good paying for this service!!

Thank you! thank you! thank you!

title: Potential to do more harm than good if you have an anxiety disorder
body:
This resorts to an eerily fear-based approach for something aimed at general self-improvement, and with such critical technical limitations.

If you don’t log into the app for a couple days it sends an acutely manipulative notification to get you to open it. This is paired with a technical limitation that neither allows you to check off tasks you completed in days prior, nor to uncheck something you tapped accidentally but didn’t complete.

Maybe it’s still a step up for people who are already glued to their phones from the moment they wake up, or are facing dangerous vices. However, studies actually show that reward-based approaches still tend to be better for learning than punishment-based ones.

Manipulative notifications paired with the limits for checking off tasks suggests poor design at best, or worse that its intention is actually to build an addiction to the app itself ($ubscription), as opposed to commitment to real-life self-improvement.

I liked it for the first couple days, but don’t want emotional punishment for not being addicted to my phone.

title: Challenges are poorly constructed but graphics are nice
body:
The challenges are poorly thought out and not very valuable. For example:

There is a “Letting go of what hurts you challenge”. Rather than tell you how give you daily guidelines or goals, the way you track it is by ticking off a box that says ‘did you let go of what hurts you?’ I found that really useless. 

There is also a challenge of ‘decluttering’. Rather than having daily goals for it, and a way to track it daily, the way that that goal is set up is that you have to do it for an entire week. For example, rather than ‘clean for 20 min today’ the goal is ‘clean for 20 min everyday this week’. I think this makes it difficult to track - the whole point of this app to progress and track your progress. There are A LOT of ‘challenges’ you can sign up for and though the intention is good, the execution and ultimate goal of BUILDING MEANINGFUL HABITS isn’t possible with them.

title: Scam, inflexible, zero response to customer
body: I liked this app at first. But the cracks started to show immediately. I couldn’t modify it to meet my needs (skip over habits I already have, for example). The app was inflexible in every way and not responsive to customer needs. And it was very unpolished and unprofessional: excellent graphics, abysmally poor writing in the text sections, and many many bugs and blank spots. I really liked the app so I gave feedback. The response was cold and ineffectual. They wanted me to catalogue every error I’d seen, and there were hundreds. Hire an editor! Hire a quality assurance person! If you’re going to charge exorbitant prices (not to mention use shady business practices to extract them), the least you can do is pay a staff person to do the skilled work of improving your product. Don’t ask your customers to do that. I checked back a year later and all of the glaring errors remained in place. This app has zero concern for a quality product, they just want to gouge people for their money. Don’t bother giving it to them.

body:
I tried this out for the free trial period because it seemed like a nice way to set and meet some personal goals. There was a small monthly fee so it seemed reasonable to test for a while. Things aren’t what they seem.
This hasn’t been a great experience. When you subscribe you are presented with a small monthly fee, after the free trial ends you are charged for an entire year and there’s no way to get a refund or sign up for month to month. So now I’m out of pocket a significant amount for this and I’m stuck with this subscription for an entire year. I might have liked this app given the chance but now I have a bad feeling about it like I have taken advantage of. Word to the wise, steer clear. There is definitely a better alternative that isn’t so shady about their payments and subscriptions.

title: Looters
body:
The worst app ever. First offs: horrible navigation. Takes forever to one goal. Feels like you are on an app for a child who needs all the colours and jumps of characters on the screen. It’s not for ADULTS. Still I was okay with it as I thought if I will be really exhausted navigating through this app I’ll stop my subscription for upcoming months.

Also. I chose a monthly subscription and they charged me for the year. I tried to raise the issue and they sent me an email with refund request form. There are number of options to select as to the reason why I am demanding a refund. Guess what, none of them works. For every option they have mentioned an excuse and said sorry we can’t refund. Then, what’s the point of giving me a form and those options. HORRIBLE SERVICE.

It clearly shows they do not intend to do good via their app. Essentially, all app developers come with underlying notion of helping or solving a problem that exists AND to make money out of it. Contrary, these guys are creating problems and making money out of it. 

DO NOT SUBSCRIBE. Find another app for creating habits. Read self help books like Robin Sharma that will help you as wel.

title: Too $$ for what it does...
body:
For the cost, I feel this app should be more complex with more in depth options.

 You should be able to customize each day in accordance to a personal schedule (if anything this causes more stress as you are less likely to complete each “habit”in the afternoon, for example, if you’re at work); Should be able to write to do lists on the app (as they encourages organization); Should be able to not just play and pause, but rewind some of the tasks, etc..., if needed...   

For $60+ you should be doing more than just ticking off good habits. :/
I think its a great concept, but needs to be more user friendly and a bit more in depth. It would be nice also, if the daily letter would be audio, in order to listen to encouragement as you complete tasks. Less time reading, more time doing.

title: Great principle but some features are poor
body: Overall the app is excellent on the principles of what it’s trying to achieve. But after a few days I really grew disappointed with a number of features that I found deficient. For instance I keep having issues visualizing the newletters. They appear blank on my app which means I can’t read them. I contacted support but reserved no feedback in over 10 days now despite having a premium plan. Also a number of proposed activities are poorly done. For instance the 7 min workout feature is extremely succinct. It give exercices to do with a timer but there is no explanation, photo or video of what to do exactly so one has to frantically google search the exercice to figure if one is doing it right. Also it is said that this exercice is scientifically proven to be efficient but there is no documentation to back it up. So essentially, beyond the rituals thing the app is simply a collection of timers with very limited content. I’m not sure it’s justified agains the cost of the app.

body: This app is so customizable, you can set your alarms and routines for any time depending on your schedule and it will wait for you even if you’re late to start it. Warning, though! Trying to take on too many tasks caused me to ignore the app for a while because when I looked at it I felt overwhelmed and disappointed with myself for how much I hadn’t done instead of how much I had. Start small and once you don’t have to think about doing those first few habits/tasks, add another until your whole day makes you feel complete and accomplished. I feel great today, and I hope you will too ❤️

title: Life changing
body:
I tried using Fabulous three times in the past and each time ending up deleting the app. I was looking for an habit tracker and the “journey based” core functionalities of Fabulous were getting in the way. But each time I would end up failing my goal of changing my habits. 

Last week was the moment I decided I would get back on my feet after a few months of suffering from depression and anxiety. “Any little step in the right direction will help”, was my mindset. Turns out that’s the mindset you need to be in to benefit from Fabulous. Turning your life around all of the sudden won’t work. You need to work on the foundation of behavioural change, and that’s what Fabulous help you do. And they do it extremely well.

title: App complete but that makes it confusing
body:

I thought that all of this was worth the very expensive price for a subscription. There are a lot of contents. 

The pricing plan is horribly complicated.
Too many types of memberships, too many different in-app rebates plus the one that you get out of the app that gives you more special. 
I ended up subscribing to 4 different memberships without knowing which one was prevailing and been charged in double. 

Very difficult to find in-app support link. 
Been struggling to remove a routine that I wanted to test and can’t even remove it and no support to help me do that. 
No support to check for the charges. 
I found a support email address by registering to the private FB group where it’s asking not to ask support questions on the group. 
I can’t believe that there is no in-pp communication system and that you have to send an email to get support.

title: Helping me through My grief
body:
I can’t believe how much this app has helped me. My daughter passed away a year ago, I’ve been on and off disability ever since. I suffer from panic attacks, nightmares, severe depression and social anxiety. I see a psychiatrist, grief councillor and psychologist but I haven’t been able to move on. I have yet to be able to get my mind to a point where I don’t feel guilty for living my life without my daughter or wanting to live without her. 

I downloaded this app on a whim hoping for some help with getting myself to do more during the day. It’s been 45 days. I’ve completed one journey and am partial through a second. At first just having a few tasks to complete everyday was daunting but now I’m doing so much more, not just more, but meaningful tasks that make me feel good about myself. 

Thank you for helping me regain some confidence and being inspired by everyday life again. I’m not better or perfect but I am seeing progress where I wasn’t before.

title: A ploy to data mine - or worse!
body:
If you realize that you've been had and THEN research these reviews, you need to understand that you MUST go to your account in the App store (click  your picture to open your profile then click "subscriptions", then "fabulous" then scroll to the bottom of the page and unsubscribe). Hopefully you'll do that before the sixth day of your "free trial" and before they trick you into "committing" unwittingly to something other than your goals. Maybe a class action for fraud will show them? 

I get it that these apps exist to buy and sell our data. I can't believe I fell for it though - it asked for a goal commitment by touching the screen. It dawned on me once my brain fart was over that it was also acquiring my fingerprint 😳 (required a sustained three second hold while it read/recorded my print). It's NOT worth it people. Learn from my stupidity! THIS is more important than the hundred bucks they're going to steal from your credit card.

I dare the developers to explain themselves by responding.
author: Patricia and Steve

title: Suggestion for the app
body:
Don’t have the very first thing say that you want us to pay $65. I tried this app once before and deleted it immediately because I can’t afford that. It wasn’t until now, several months later, when I came across it again I saw a comment that you can enjoy and benefit even without in app purchases. You owe that person a thank you because if something is beneficial to my health, I can save up money for it. There’s a SLIGHT chance (because you pushed subs it’s slight) that I will pay in the future because I will already have seen some of what the app offers. 
I wonder how many people that 7 day TRIAL page scared off. 
From what I’ve seen so far, in the app, it does look like it will help. But it doesn’t look good to demand money up front. Make it a paid app or make it very clear that it is an option. Otherwise you’re not helping everyone who needs it, just the ones who are stable enough to work the hours necessary to have an extra $60 just on hand. Some people are like me and need help learning how to function with mental health and abuse. Everything about your app suggests that you do actually want to help people, even people like me. People like me are sometimes poor. I’m not ashamed to admit it about myself, but others aren’t as broken as I am. 
Not complaining that you have the subscription plan. I’m sure it does have a lot of features that help. But make it clear that it is optional, not required to use your app. You’ll help more people. 
Sorry for the rambling rant

(Keep in mind that each email takes a day for them to get back to you, so by now I’m into it three days). Today I got an email saying something along the lines of: “thanks for telling us this. We actually can’t refund you anything. You need to contact apple.” Which I did, as well as my cc company (waiting on hold forever was not-so-“fabulous”).  Thank you for the enormous waste of time.
